title: “GOD ASKED FOR HIS SON.”
paragraphs: “GOD ASKED FOR HIS SON.”

Not his money.
Not his livestock.
Not his reputation.
His son.
And heaven went silent.
Would you still trust God?
Family, lean in.
The Climb — Book of Genesis 22
God speaks to Abraham:
“Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love…”

Do you feel that?
Heaven names the wound before pressing it.

The promised child.
The miracle laughter.
The future wrapped in flesh.
Some scholars interpret this as the ultimate test of covenant loyalty — not because God delights in pain, but because He exposes what owns our hearts.
And Abraham rose early.

No argument recorded.
No delay.
Just obedience.
Three days up a mountain with a question echoing in his chest.

Isaac turns and asks,
“Father… where is the lamb?”
That question split history in half.
The Tension
Abraham binds the promise.

Rough rope against young wrists.
Wood beneath trembling knees.
Fire in his hand.
Knife in the other.
And heaven still says nothing.
This is the moment most people leave God.

When obedience feels like betrayal.
When the promise looks like it’s bleeding.
When faith smells like smoke.
Would you still trust Him?
The Pivot

At the last second —
“Abraham! Abraham!”
The knife stops mid-air.

A ram caught in the thicket.
Substitute provided.

Jehovah-Jireh.
“The Lord will provide.”
But don’t miss it — this wasn’t just about Isaac.
This mountain was whispering about another Son.

Centuries later, another Father would walk up another hill.
This time there would be no voice stopping the blade.
Jesus Christ carried the wood on His back.

No ram in the thicket.
No substitute for Him.
He was the substitute.

For you.
For me.
Where Abraham was stopped, God the Father was not.
Because redemption demanded blood.
And grace demanded love.
Close the Loop
You ask, “Would I trust God?”
Here’s the deeper question:
Do you trust the God who did not spare His own Son for you?

The test in Genesis 22 was never about cruelty.
It was prophecy soaked in mercy.

Abraham received his son back.
We receive salvation because the Father gave His.

Your Isaac — your dream, relationship, career, reputation —
Place it on the altar.

Not because God wants to destroy it.
But because He wants to prove He is better.

Today, surrender what you’re gripping.
And trust the God who provides the Lamb.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
